filename: Zero-shot learning of aerosol optical properties with graph neural networks.pdf
title: Zero-shot learning of aerosol optical properties with graph neural networks
processes: black carbon fractal aggregate optical properties
parameterization_target: aerosol optical properties (scattering, extinction, and absorption efficiencies; asymmetry parameter; scattering phase matrix elements)
testbed_rationale: The study generated an open-access benchmark dataset of black carbon fractal aggregates and exact MSTM electromagnetic calculations published on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.5108834) with corresponding open-source code on GitHub.
pain_points: Exact electromagnetic solvers like MSTM are computationally prohibitive (hours to days for large aggregates) for direct use in atmospheric models or online retrievals.
Conventional machine learning algorithms (e.g., SVM, standard NNs) fail to generalize to morphological parameters outside their training distribution.
High relative error (MAPE) occurs for scattering efficiency at very small size parameters (Xv = 0.1) due to small absolute values.
extraction_notes: Author first names are given as initials 'K. D.' and 'P.' in the document text. The aggregate scale is single-particle microphysics (cluster of nanospheres).
